page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.6xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock speed of 2.9 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 24 dedicated virtual CPUs (spanning 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled) and 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is absent on this instance, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage, while the network interface delivers an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results place general compute capabilities within standard expectations for 24-vCPU systems, recording a PassMark CPU score of 29,197.78 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,181.0. Memory subsystem throughput shows balanced performance, delivering 135.11 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB read operations and 65.44 GB/sec on writes. Synthetic caching and retrieval tasks demonstrate strong throughput, producing 23.67 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. Small language model text generation achieves 298.41 tokens per second on a 135M model, though larger medium models scale down to 15.85 tokens per second.

Due to the absence of bundled local NVMe storage and discrete hardware acceleration, the instance trades high local IOPS capability for large memory density per core. Cost efficiency is primarily driven by its memory capacity, providing substantial RAM for large working sets without paying for specialized accelerators. Appropriate workloads include in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached, relational databases requiring substantial buffer pool allocations, enterprise ERP applications, and in-memory analytical pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs on 12 physical cores and 192.0 GB of memory, driven by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor at 2.9 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with the KVM hypervisor, it provides an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio supported by 48 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 VNNI vector extensions. The instance includes an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and contains no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on remote block storage for persistence. Benchmark performance reflects consistent mid-tier execution across CPU and memory tests, scoring 29,197.78 in PassMark CPU and handling 23.67 million Redis SET operations per second. With its dense RAM profile and dedicated compute threads, ecs.r7se.6xlarge fits in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, relational database servers, and memory-bound enterprise data processing workloads.
